title: Why CPU Branch Prediction Makes Your Code 10x Faster Behind the Scenes — Engineering Cheat Sheet
subtitle: Harnessing speculative execution to eliminate pipeline stalls and latency.
summary: Branch prediction allows CPUs to guess execution paths before conditional results are known, keeping the instruction pipeline full. Mastering this minimizes costly flushes and pipeline stalls, directly impacting high-performance system throughput.

key_concepts.name: Pipeline Stalls
key_concepts.detail: Occur when the CPU must wait for branch resolution before fetching subsequent instructions, essentially idling the execution units and incurring a massive latency penalty per misprediction.

key_concepts.name: Speculative Execution
key_concepts.detail: The CPU guesses the outcome of a conditional branch and executes instructions ahead of time, discarding results if wrong or committing them if the guess is correct.

key_concepts.name: Branch Target Buffer (BTB)
key_concepts.detail: A high-speed hardware cache storing addresses of previous jump targets, allowing the CPU to predict not just the branch outcome, but also the destination address.

code_cheatsheet.explanation: Provides compiler hints to structure code so the most likely branch occupies the fall-through path, improving instruction cache locality and branch predictor efficiency.
Sorting input data before conditional processing makes branches highly predictable, allowing the CPU to execute loops with near-zero misprediction overhead.

best_practices: Prefer branchless logic using conditional moves (CMOV) or bitwise operations for performance-critical hot paths.
Order if-else chains based on frequency of occurrence, placing the most common case in the first block.
Minimize complex nested conditionals within tight loops to prevent exhausting the Branch Target Buffer capacity.
Profile code with hardware counters (e.g., perf) to identify misprediction ratios before prematurely optimizing branch logic.

interview_qa.question: Why does sorting an array significantly speed up a loop containing a simple 'if' condition?
interview_qa.answer: Sorting minimizes the frequency of conditional transitions, creating a pattern the Branch Predictor can easily track. This prevents pipeline flushes caused by unexpected branch outcomes, allowing the CPU to sustain maximum throughput via speculative execution.
